message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to some of the most highly‑rated sushi spots in Los Angeles—spanning classic omakase experiences, modern fusion concepts, and hidden gems that locals swear by. All of them consistently score above 4★ on major review sites (Google, Yelp, Eater) and offer something unique whether you’re after traditional nigiri, creative rolls, or a memorable dining experience.

| # | Restaurant | Neighborhood | Style & Highlights | Price Range* | Why It Stands Out |
|---|------------|--------------|--------------------|-------------|------------------|
| **1** | **Sushi Ginza Onodera** | West Hollywood | Traditional Japanese omakase; seasonal fish flown from Japan; meticulous plating | $250–$350 per person (omakase only) | Awarded “Best Omakase” by *Eater LA*. Chef Masahiro Onodera brings decades of Tokyo expertise. |
| **2** | **Kazuya** | Downtown L.A. | Contemporary kaiseki + sushi bar; emphasis on local ingredients blended with Japanese techniques | $150–$200 per person | Known for its intimate setting and chef‑curated tasting menus featuring both sashimi and innovative dishes. |
| **3** | **Matsuhisa** | Beverly Hills | Nobu‑style upscale sushi & Peruvian-Japanese fusion | $80–$120 per dish | Celebrity hotspot; signature black cod miso and truffle-infused rolls keep it fresh. |
| **4** | **Umi** | Santa Monica | Classic Edo‑Tokyo sushi with a focus on sustainability; open kitchen view | $70–$110 per plate | Transparent sourcing, including farm‑to‑table fish; great for families and groups. |
| **5** | **Shin Soba** | Koreatown | Authentic soba noodles plus high‑quality sushi; small but cozy | $25–$45 per meal | A neighborhood favorite offering affordable yet authentic sushi without compromising quality. |
| **6** | **Oishii** | Silver Lake | Trendy spot blending street‑food vibes with premium sushi | $30–$60 per roll | Popular among millennials; offers inventive rolls like the “Bacon Maki.” |
| **7** | **Tatsu** | Culver City | Hidden gem known for its house‑made wasabi and simple, honest sushi | $35–$55 per plate | Small menu, big flavor; perfect for those who appreciate minimalism. |

\*Prices reflect typical ranges at the time of writing; check each venue’s website for current pricing and reservation policies.

### How to Pick Your Spot

| Preference | Recommended Choice(s) |
|-----------|-----------------------|
| **Purely Omnaka** | Sushi Ginza Onodera, Kazuya |
| **Fusion/Trendy** | Matsuhisa, Umi, Oishii |
| **Budget Friendly** | Shin Soba, Tatsu |
| **Family / Group** | Umi (open kitchen), Matsuhisa (large tables) |
| **Hidden Local Favorite** | Tatsu, Shin Soba |

### Practical Tips

1. **Reservations:** For places like Sushi Ginza Onodera and Kazuya, book months ahead via their websites or phone lines.  
2. **Dress Code:** Many high-end spots enforce smart casual attire; bring your wallet ready because prices climb quickly once you order the omakase.  
3. **Allergies & Dietary Needs:** Call ahead – many chefs will accommodate gluten-free or vegan requests when possible.  
4. **Timing:** Lunch hours often see fewer crowds; dinner reservations fill up fast, especially during weekends.  

---

#### Quick Links

- [Sushi Ginza Onodera](https://www.sushiginzayonodera.com/)
- [Kazuya](http://kazuya.la/) *(check for updated address)* 
- [Matsuhisa](https://matsuhisabeverlyhills.com/)
- [Umi](https://umilacompany.com/)
- [Shin Soba](https://shinsobamc.com/)
- [Oishii](https://oishiila.com/)
- [Tatsu](https://tattusushi.com/)

Enjoy exploring LA’s vibrant sushi scene! If you’d like deeper dives into any particular area (e.g., vegetarian-friendly sushi, weekend brunch combos, or family‑friendly venues), let me know—I’m happy to tailor the list further.
